papers.title_in_file: Learning complexity of many-body quantum sign structures through the lens of Boolean Fourier analysis
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (start), Section 3 learning algorithms (Hadamard and Fourier learning results, Figs 10 and 12), Section 4 Discussion; Section 2 and the appendix were skimmed by keyword only.
papers.what_it_is: A physics paper that analyzes ground-state sign structures of frustrated spin-1/2 Heisenberg models with Boolean Fourier analysis and proposes Hadamard and Fourier learning to predict signs.

assertions.value: The authors report that their Hadamard learning and Fourier learning algorithms dramatically outperform neural networks at supervised sign structure reconstruction, and that for the 24-spin Kagome lattice Hadamard learning does so in the frustrated regime as measured by sign overlap.
quotes: In Fig. 10, we present results for the 24-spin Kagome lattice. One can see that Hadamard learning dramatically outperforms neural networks in the frustrated regime,
We have introduced Hadamard and Fourier learning as explicit algorithms for supervised sign structure reconstruction. Both dramatically outperform neural networks in this task
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small (24-spin) systems.
assertions.reader_inference: The task is classical sign prediction for spin ground states, not a quantum-hardware workload; the comparison is against neural networks only.

assertions.value: The authors state that they studied ground states of 24-spin Heisenberg models on square, triangular, and Kagome lattices, with frustration controlled by J2/J1.
quotes: we studied ground states of 24-spin Heisenberg models on square, triangular, and Kagome lattices with varying frustration levels controlled by J2/J1
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own system sizes and models (Section 4).

assertions.value: The authors state that Fourier learning faces scalability issues due to exponential coefficient estimation requirements, and that practical integration of the two algorithms with variational methods requires consideration.
assertions.anchor: Section 3.2 closing paragraph and Section 4 Discussion
quotes: While Fourier learning faces scalability issues due to exponential coefficient estimation requirements
but their practical integration with variational methods requires consideration.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated limit, Section 4 and end of Section 3.

papers.title_in_file: End-to-End Demonstration of Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks for Steel Microstructure Image Augmentation on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusions, QPU section by keyword; methods and results figures not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An IonQ and Hyundai paper that trains a quantum circuit at the input layer of a classical Wasserstein GAN to generate steel EBSD images, in simulation and on a trapped-ion QPU.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with respect to maximum mean discrepancy score, the hybrid quantum-classical WGAN improves over classical Bernoulli GANs in 70% of samples.
quotes: With respect to maximum mean discrepancy score, we find that the hybrid quantum-classical WGAN improves over classical Bernoulli GANs in 70% of samples.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract compares against classical Bernoulli GANs while the conclusions compare against a classical WGAN of the same structure; the 70% figure is a share of cases, not a size of gain.

assertions.value: The authors report relative improvements from the classical solution between 22% and 99% for ferrite images and between -45% and 150% for bainite images, with positive relative improvements on 70% of the cases.
quotes: Experiments showed relative improvements from the classical solution between 22% and 99% for the models used to generate ferrite images, and between -45% and 150% for the models used to generate bainite images, with positive relative improvements on 70% of the cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, noiseless simulation across hyperparameters.
assertions.reader_inference: The bainite range includes a negative improvement, so the hybrid model was worse than the classical one in some cases.

assertions.value: The authors state that both models were trained from limited image datasets with a relatively small number of qubits encoding the latent vector, and that their demonstration was based on only 12 qubits.
quotes: Both models were trained from limited image datasets and with a relatively small number of qubits encoding the latent vector.
While our demonstration was based on only 12 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated scope, Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that, despite gate level noise on the trapped-ion QPU, the hybrid quantum-classical model reproduced the trends of the noiseless simulations, training faster and generating images with higher quality than its classical counterpart.
quotes: the hybrid quantum-classical model reproduced the trends showed in the noiseless simulations, training faster and generating images with higher quality than its classical counterpart
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one hardware run, authors' own claim.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper authors include a vendor (IonQ), so the hardware result is partly a vendor demonstration.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Mackey-Glass results section, Rydberg section (start), Conclusions; memory and NARMA sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that adds memory to quantum reservoir computing by classical post-processing of quantum measurements and tests it in simulation on an Ising model and a Rydberg atom array.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid model achieves a substantially longer prediction time on the chaotic Mackey-Glass series than previously reported approaches, predicting up to approximately 700 steps.
quotes: where it demonstrates significantly enhanced predictive capabilities and achieves a substantially longer prediction time, outperforming previously reported approaches.
It is seen that the system can predict up to approximately 700 steps, which is significantly higher than recent literature results
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, comparison with literature values.
assertions.reader_inference: Results come from numerical simulation of the Hamiltonians, not from quantum hardware; the 700-step figure is for one specific case shown in Fig. 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that they tested the model on two physical platforms, a fully connected Ising model and a Rydberg atom array, and that each plotted VPT point is based on 30 different realizations of the Hamiltonian.
quotes: We tested our model on two physical platforms: a fully connected Ising model and a Rydberg atom array
For each point, the mean value and standard deviation of the mean are shown, based on 30 different realizations of the Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup, abstract and Fig. 5 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that their approach was designed to mitigate challenges of purely quantum reservoir computing, such as requiring multiple copies of the quantum system.
quotes: Our approach was designed to mitigate the challenges associated with purely quantum reservoir computing, such as requiring multiple copies of the quantum system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' design claim.

papers.title_in_file: Towards practical and massively parallel quantum computing emulation for quantum chemistry
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results scaling paragraph, Discussion, Summary paragraph; methods and appendix sections not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A paper presenting a matrix-product-state VQE simulator combined with DMET embedding, run on the New Sunway supercomputer for quantum chemistry emulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that their largest simulation reaches 1000 qubits and a performance of 216.9 PFLOPS on a new Sunway supercomputer.
quotes: Our largest simulation reaches 1000 qubits, and a performance of 216.9 PFLOPS is achieved on a new Sunway supercomputer
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical performance figure from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The 1000-qubit run is a one-shot energy evaluation, not a converged VQE; see the scope assertion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MPS-VQE simulator scales up to 1000 qubits for one-shot energy evaluation and to 92 qubits for converged VQE emulation, with the maximally allowed bond dimension set to D = 128.
assertions.anchor: Section III Discussions; Section II results on the hydrogen chain
quotes: the MPS-VQE simulator scales up to 1000 qubits for oneshot energy evaluation and to 92 qubits for converged VQE emulation
The maximally allowed bond dimension is set to be D = 128
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own scope, Discussion.

assertions.value: The authors state that they limited themselves to the physically motivated UCCSD ansatz.
quotes: Although we have limited ourselves to the physical motivated UCCSD ansatz
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated limit, Discussions.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in a protein-ligand interaction application for drug discovery, they can obtain decent results using VQE that are comparable with the experimental observations.
quotes: we can obtain descent results using VQE, which are comparable with the experimental observations
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim; the quantitative comparison is in a table not read.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is from classical emulation of VQE, not from a quantum computer.

papers.title_in_file: Trainability of Dissipative Perceptron-Based Quantum Neural Networks
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2005.12458v2 (10 Jun 2022); the file name carries 2020-05.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, main-text theorems and Conclusions; the supplementary proofs were located but not read line by line.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proves barren plateaus can arise in dissipative perceptron-based quantum neural networks and gives conditions under which they are avoided.

assertions.value: The paper proves that dissipative quantum neural networks are not immune to barren plateaus, and that DQNNs with deep global perceptrons are untrainable despite the dissipative nature of the architecture.
quotes: we here analytically prove that DQNNs are not immune to barren plateaus.
DQNNs with deep global perceptrons are untrainable despite the dissipative nature of the architecture.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 in the main text, proofs in the supplementary material.
assertions.reader_inference: The theorems assume the perceptrons form independent 2-designs, so the result is a statement about random-initialization trainability.

assertions.value: The authors show that for shallow and local perceptrons, employing global cost functions leads to barren plateaus, while using local costs avoids them.
quotes: for shallow and local perceptrons, employing global cost functions leads to barren plateaus, while using local costs avoids them.
assertions.certainty_reason: Main-text analysis of shallow local perceptrons; the local-cost, logarithmic-depth case rests on a cited result.
assertions.reader_inference: Trainability without a barren plateau is not the same as a proof that the network solves the learning task.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results are completely general for DQNN architectures, covering arbitrary numbers of hidden layers and general perceptrons acting on any number of qubits.
quotes: We note that our results are completely general for DQNN architectures, e.g., covering arbitrary numbers of hidden layers and general perceptrons acting on any number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own scope, Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors state that an earlier reference, based on small scale numerical experiments, speculated that dissipative quantum neural networks do not suffer from the barren plateau problem.
quotes: based on small scale numerical experiments, it was speculated that dissipative quantum neural networks do not suffer from the barren plateau (vanishing gradient) problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited result, which this paper then contradicts.

papers.title_in_file: Evidence of Scaling Advantage for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm on a Classically Intractable Problem
papers.version_note: File is the paper itself (arXiv 2308.02342v2), not only a code listing; the file name says Code-from-Evidence.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, main results on scaling, Table 1 caption, Discussion, start of Methods; supplementary information and hardware sections not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A JPMorgan Chase, Quantinuum and Argonne paper that simulates QAOA on the LABS problem up to 40 qubits and fits the time-to-solution scaling against classical solvers.

assertions.value: The authors report that in noiseless simulations with up to 40 qubits the runtime of QAOA with fixed parameters scales better than branch-and-bound solvers for the LABS problem.
quotes: We perform noiseless simulations with up to 40 qubits and observe that the runtime of QAOA with fixed parameters scales better than branch-and-bound solvers
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical scaling fit from one study on instances up to 40 variables.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is of fitted exponents from simulation, not of wall-clock time on a quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors report that the combination of QAOA with quantum minimum-finding gives the best empirical scaling of any algorithm for the LABS problem, and that TTS of QAOA grows as 1.46N at constant QAOA depth p = 12.
quotes: The combination of QAOA with quantum minimum-finding gives the best empirical scaling of any algorithm for the LABS problem.
that TTS of QAOA grows as 1.46N with problem size at constant QAOA depth p = 12
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical fit from simulation; the quantum minimum-finding scaling is derived by combining the fit with a known routine.
assertions.reader_inference: The 1.46N notation is the base-to-the-power-N form with the superscript lost in text extraction.

assertions.value: The authors state that evaluating time to solution is only possible when the solution is known, that is only up to 66 variables, and that further improvements in quantum error correction and hardware are necessary to implement quantum minimum-finding augmented with QAOA.
quotes: First, evaluating time to solution is only possible when the solution is known, i.e. only up to 66 variables.
However, further improvements in quantum error correction and hardware are necessary to implement the quantum minimum-finding augmented with QAOA.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated limits, Discussion.
assertions.reader_inference: The speedup rests on an idealized fault-tolerant quantum computer and an extrapolation beyond the fitted sizes.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network for phytoplankton classification
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 4.1 dataset, Section 4.2 comparison with CNN and ResNet, Conclusion; ansatz-circuit section skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that builds hybrid quantum-classical convolutional and residual networks (QCCNN, QCResNet) for phytoplankton image classification and compares them with classical templates.

assertions.value: The authors report that the classification accuracy of QCCNN-1 is about 93.0%, close to that of CNN, and that the classification accuracy of QCResNet-1 is 93.2%, higher than the 91.9% of ResNet.
quotes: The classification accuracy of QCCNN-1 is about 93.0%, which is close to that of CNN.
The classification accuracy of QCResNet-1 is 93.2%, higher than the 91.9% of ResNet.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a small dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: A 1.3 point gap on a 600-image test set from numerical experiments is not shown with an error bar or repeat runs in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors report that QCCNN converges much faster than CNN and QCResNet-1 converges faster than ResNet, while QCResNet-2 has worse performance than ResNet, which they take to show a large impact of the replacement scheme of quantum convolutional layers.
quotes: the prominent feature of QCCNN is that it converges much faster than CNN
QCResNet-1 converges faster than ResNet
However, QCResNet-2 has worse performance than ResNet, which again imply the large impact of the replacement scheme of quantum convolutional layers on the model performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The better result depends on which layers were replaced, so it is not a general quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dataset comprises 1200 images of 4 kinds of phytoplankton, divided unbiasedly into training and testing subsets with 600 images each.
quotes: The dataset comprises of 1200 images and contains 4 kinds of phytoplankton
The 1200 images are divided unbiasedly into the training and testing subset with 600 images each.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own dataset, Section 4.1.
assertions.reader_inference: A 4-class, 1200-image set is small, and the models were run by numerical experiment, not on quantum hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Influence of Data Dimensionality Reduction Methods on the Effectiveness of Quantum Machine Learning Models
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, dataset and simulation setup sections, discussion paragraphs and Conclusion; the per-table results were not read cell by cell.
papers.what_it_is: A study of how PCA, truncated SVD, autoencoder and t-SNE data reduction change the measured performance of quantum neural networks and quantum kernel methods on generated datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that data dimensionality reduction results in skewed performance metric values, with a difference in the accuracy range of 14% to 48% between using and not using data reduction.
quotes: We consistently observed the difference in the accuracy range of 14% to 48% amongst these models, using data reduction and not using it.
the usage of data dimensionality reduction methods results in skewed performance metric values
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on generated datasets in classical simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The direction of the gap differs by model type, so the range does not mean reduction always lowers accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that Quantum Neural Networks benefit from data dimensionality reduction methods, while Quantum Support Vector Machines experience decreased performance due to their reliance on classical Support Vector Classifier components.
quotes: we can conclusively state that Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) benefit from data dimensionality reduction methods, while Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVMs) experience decreased performance due to their reliance on classical Support Vector Classifier (SVC) components.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; authors' interpretation of cause.
assertions.reader_inference: The Conclusion adds that the QNN gain cannot be fully attributed to the quantum model.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have not found definitive evidence identifying which reduction method is compatible with a specific ansatz or the optimal percentage of reduction for achieving the best results.
quotes: we have not found definitive evidence identifying which method is compatible with a specific ansatz or the optimal percentage of reduction for achieving the best results.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own stated limit, discussion before the Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experimentation was conducted on several datasets for binary classification and that the simulations were implemented using the Pennylane Framework.
quotes: This experimentation was conducted on several datasets for binary classification.
The simulations were implemented using the Pennylane Framework
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The datasets are generated, not real-world, and the circuits were simulated classically, so the findings may not carry to real data or hardware.
